back_translation: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“As for you, son of man, take up a lament concerning Tyre.
Say to Tyre, who dwells at the gateway of the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands, the Lord GOD says this: O Tyre, you have said, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’
Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders perfected your beauty.
They built all your planks with cypress from Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; they made your deck of pine from the coasts of Cyprus, inlaid with ivory.
Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail, serving also as your banner; blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah were your awning.
The men of Sidon and Arvad were your oarsmen; your skilled men, O Tyre, were aboard you as your captains.
The elders of Gebal and its skilled men were aboard you as caulkers repairing your leaks; all the ships of the sea and their sailors came alongside you to barter for your merchandise.
Men of Persia, Lud, and Put served in your army as your warriors; they hung their shields and helmets in you and gave you splendor.
Men of Arvad and your army manned your walls all around, and Gammadim were in your towers; they hung their shields on your walls all around and perfected your beauty.
Tarshish was your trading partner because of your abundant goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants; they exchanged slaves and bronze vessels for your merchandise.
The men of Beth-togarmah exchanged horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
The men of Dedan were your clients; many coastlands were your market; they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
Aram was your trading partner because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your wares.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, cakes, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.
Damascus was your trading partner because of your many products and your abundant wealth, exchanging wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
Dan and Javan from Uzal brought goods to exchange for your wares; wrought iron, cassia, and sweet cane were among your merchandise.
Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers, trading with you in lambs, rams, and goats.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; they exchanged the finest of all spices, every kind of precious stone, and gold for your wares.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
They traded with you in your marketplace in fine garments, blue cloth, embroidered work, multicolored carpets, and cords tightly twisted and bound.
The ships of Tarshish were the caravans carrying your merchandise; so you were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
Your oarsmen brought you out onto the great waters, but the east wind will wreck you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth, wares, and merchandise, your sailors and captains, your caulkers and traders, all your warriors who are in you, along with all the crowd within you, will sink into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.
The surrounding lands will shake at the sound of your captains' cry.
All who handle the oar will come down from their ships; the sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore.
They will raise their voices wailing over you and cry out bitterly; they will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads bald for you and gird themselves with sackcloth; they will weep over you with anguish of soul and bitter mourning.
As they wail and lament over you, they will take up a lament concerning you: ‘Who was ever like Tyre, silenced in the midst of the sea?’
When your wares went out to the seas, you satisfied many peoples; you enriched the kings of the earth with your abundant wealth and merchandise.
Now you are wrecked by the seas, in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all the crowd within you have gone down with you.
All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled over you; their kings shudder with horror, their faces contorted with fear.
The merchants among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end, and you will be no more forever.”
